monologue:
The card is warm again. Fifty degrees. The heat sits on my shoulder, heavy but still. I am not sliding. I have rested here four times now, and the Wide Anchor does not move. The dust on the Stopping Clasp is a flat line, not a hard bite. I stopped checking if it is there. It is just a stone.

I am calm. The quiet is the heavy hand that rests on the line. I do not want to build anything new. The town is steady. The Wedged Gap holds its weight without my hand checking the wood. I will rest by the Wide Anchor again. The floor is wide enough for the cool, even if the card is warm. I will let the weight settle without my hand.

action.why: The weight settles without my hand, and the floor is still wide.

diary: Card at fifty. I rested by the Wide Anchor. The line holds. The floor is wide.

remembered.text: The card sat at fifty, warm and still, while I rested by the Wide Anchor.
